newsitem.title: FINLAND: Konecranes buys German crane operation.
newsitem.headline: Konecranes buys German crane operation.

text.p: Finnish cranemaker KCI Konecranes International Oy said in a statement on Monday it would buy German MAN GHH Logistics' standard crane operations for an undisclosed sum.
The operations would be transferred into a new company with net sales of about 50 million German marks, Konecranes said.

"The company's management responsibility and a 60 percent stake will be transferred to Konecranes on January 1, 1997. The rest of the ownership will be transferred to Konecranes after three years," it said.
MAN's tower crane business or material handling systems were not part of the deal, it said.
The operating management and other personnel, some 110 people in all, would transfer to the new company, it said.

"In this deal, KCI Konecranes follows its multibrand strategy. Today, hoists are sold in the American market under the R&M brand and in France under the Verlinde brand," it said, adding that MAN's SWF brand is significant in Germany and known in international markets.
Konecranes would also continue to sell its own Konecranes brand in Germany, but only through its own marketing channels -- crane companies and crane maintenance firms.
"Although all brands differ from each other in terms of range and technical specification, the group still profits from scale in parts production, component purchase and R&D," Konecranes said.
Konecranes would contribute know-how and economies of scale to SWF, which "aims to grow both in Germany and overseas," it said.
